agent_notes: The preposition 'itanu is 'with us', not 'upon us' as in the KJV and ASV. YLT has 'with us'. I kept 'with' in the literal layer and used 'upon' only in the dramatic layer. The verbs are imperfects read as wishes (jussive sense), which is how KJV, ASV and BBE take them. YLT reads them as plain statements ('God doth favour us').

Elohim here is glossed 'God', not YHWH. The Elohistic Psalter (Pss 42-83) replaces the divine name with Elohim, so the echo of the priestly blessing (Num 6:24-26), which has YHWH as subject, appears here with Elohim. I mention the echo in the commentary as my own reading.

agent_notes: Replaced the chiasm sentence, as requested, with the order the Hebrew has: nations glad, peoples judged on level ground, nations on the earth led. agent_notes: Reviewer request applied: the literal layer now reads 'may he bless us, God, our God', carrying exactly the two words אֱלֹהִים אֱלֹהֵינוּ with no extra 'God'.

Tense of נָתְנָה: a plain perfect, 'has given'. Translations split between past (ASV, YLT), future (KJV, Webster) and a wish. I kept the perfect in the literal layer and let the dramatic layer read it as a harvest already in hand, the ground for the blessing asked in the next clause. The tense of יְבָרְכֵנוּ is also ambiguous (imperfect: 'will bless' or 'may he bless'); I took it as a jussive-flavoured wish, matching the refrain of verse 2 (יְבָרְכֵנוּ). This is my reading; the commentaries in the packet do not settle it.
Glosses 5 and 6: STEPBible tags both אֱלֹהִים and אֱלֹהֵינוּ as deity.yhwh. The word here is Elohim, not the name YHWH, so I rendered 'God' in both layers, not 'LORD'.
